constraint_introduced: The proposer runs terminal-side and writes the ledger through shared/ledger.py with direct file access. The viewer renders a proposal and the recorded calls, and computes no relationship of its own.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: The approach belongs in this repository and at this layer. ADR-0001 holds the viewer to one self-contained file under a content policy that blocks every external request, and the browser cannot run git. A relationship computed from a textual conflict is therefore terminal work by construction, not by preference. Placing the proposer in the pr plugin, next to the modes that already read git, follows the boundary the family already keeps.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: The approach helps. ADR-0020 records that viewer/index.html is the repository's largest maintenance problem, and it is decided and not executed. Every rejected option in intent.alternatives put its cost inside that file. This one puts the computation in a new terminal-side mode and leaves the viewer with a render-only job, so the deck does not enlarge the file before its own split has run.

findings.question: pattern
findings.text: New pattern, not a duplicate. ADR-0018 decided one derived record index that resolves every join between records, and it lists no pull-request-to-pull-request join. The braid projection adds that join through a review unit rather than through a pairwise edge, which is consistent with how the index already joins an epic to a pull request through its design.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: A risk the approach carries. ADR-0019 fixed the ledger vocabulary at comment, reply, and state, and fold_threads skips a line it does not recognise. A region verdict and a disposition are neither, so each needs its own projection. Two projections over one append-only file is the shape ADR-0019 intended, and nothing enforces that a future reader of the ledger handles both.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: The transitivity of a union-find fold is the most likely source of a wrong record. A reviewer who groups A with B at one region and B with C at another has made two statements, and the fold makes a third they did not. Either label the transitive edge as derived, or stop the projection at pairwise edges.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: Deferring the design-level join to inflight-record-store is coherent, because that design already owns the pull-request entity gap. It leaves this design with textual conflict as its only strong relationship signal, and textual conflict needs a branch fetch. A cohort whose branches cannot be fetched gets an empty proposal, and the deck must say so on screen rather than render a confident empty state.

regret_risk: The approach does work on the reviewer's behalf before they arrive, which is what makes it worth building and what makes it dangerous. A proposed partition is the first thing the reviewer reads, so a wrong proposal anchors them, and the mechanic that makes the Cut cheap, treating an untouched bracket as an accepted decision, converts that anchoring into a recorded call nobody examined. If this design ships and the proposal turns out to be wrong more often than it is right, the team lives with a review surface that manufactures agreement faster than the old one manufactured backlog. The first epic exists to test the cheaper half of that claim before any of it is built, and nothing in this design tests the anchoring half.
